dialect.detail: Uses '$ SET SOURCEFORMAT "FREE"' compiler directive typical of Micro Focus/Visual COBOL; authored on Ideone which supports GnuCOBOL but directive syntax leans Micro Focus
evidence: Function ORD / Function CHAR / Function UPPER-CASE / Function LENGTH

purpose.domain_detail: Caesar cipher encryption/decryption demonstration written as a student exercise
purpose.summary: Implements a Caesar cipher in COBOL with three subprograms: ENCRYPT shifts each uppercase letter by a given amount, DECRYPT reverses the shift, and SOLVE brute-forces all 26 possible shifts. The main program IDEONE iterates over a table of test strings and calls each subprogram in turn.

notable_features: Multiple nested PROGRAM-ID / END PROGRAM blocks (nested/contained programs)
Use of intrinsic functions: ORD, CHAR, UPPER-CASE, LENGTH
OCCURS with INDEXED BY and REDEFINES for string table
LINKAGE SECTION with PROCEDURE DIVISION USING
Shift-by-1 Caesar cipher with wrap-around logic using ASCII ordinal values
Heavy use of inline comments with *> style
verdict.notes: The $ SET SOURCEFORMAT directive is Micro Focus syntax but the code was likely compiled on Ideone (GnuCOBOL). The data structure for eTestStrTable has a PIC clause on the 01 level alongside 02-level children, which is a structural oddity. The program has several commented-out lines and debug DISPLAYs, consistent with a student learning exercise. Author and date are explicitly stated in the source.
